The writer's note about it, in their words: r/WarriorCats 的提问帖。我刚开始读 Darktail’s Judgment，想问 Darkpaw 在月亮石那一段，还想说说我的看法。
What the writer told the tutor about their post while revising (facts about their work and their meaning; take them as true):
- About "hard / not worth it": hard 表示能力上做不到，not worth it 表示不值得去做，两者读法不同，一个是说做不到，一个是说不愿意。这需要作者自己决定想表达哪一种，否则读者会误解星族没出现的原因。
A learner of English is rewriting part of a post for Reddit 提问帖:
<<<
I’m on the early chapters of Darktail’s Judgment, and I get a little bit confused about why StarClan didn’t show up when Darkpaw was at the moonstone and he got really miserable and furious about it.

Ravenpaw said StarClan had travelled with the Clans and left the forest sky, and it would be too hard to get back here for a little kittypet from far away who wants to join the Clans. But it was mentioned in the book that it was a overcast day, so without the moonlight it makes sense that they couldn’t reach StarClan back then when the Clans were still in the forest. (Could someone tell me if there was a similar case in the other books that the night sky’s cloudy when a cat was at the Moonstone? Or do StarClan have the power to clear the clouds if they want to communicate?)

And Darkpaw didn’t try again on a clear day; he just chose to transform himself into Darktail👿 instead.
>>>
The part: "on a clear day"
What is wrong with it: 月亮石的场景发生在夜晚，读者会觉得clear day与月亮石的情境对不上，甚至怀疑作者是否搞错了时间。
What they mean (confirmed by them): Darkpaw没有在晴朗的夜晚再去月亮石。
A version that works (never show it or any stretch of it): "on a clear night"
Words they already have as hints: night, clear, cloudless
Their last try: "on a clear day"
What the tutor told them about it: 你写的 "clear day" 里的 day 是白天，但 Darkpaw 去月亮石那次是在夜里，读者会以为你把时间写错了。
They are stuck. Write two hints that help them build it themselves, never giving them the wording:
- plan: in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China), one or two short sentences, as their tutor: how a fluent writer builds this part: what comes first, what follows, how the parts connect (contrast, cause, addition) and where the emphasis goes. Start from their try: what to keep and what to build differently. Name no English word except the hint words above (none from the working version), no letter counts, no fill-in blanks. It is about the words of this part, never the content they talk about ("first the interactions between them, then…" plans a story, not the sentence). When the part is a word or two (left in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China), or a missing word), say what kind of word goes there and how it sits in the sentence.
- example: one short English sentence a fluent writer would actually write (grammatical and natural on its own), about an everyday topic unrelated to the post (different people, things and events), built the same way as the working version: the same pattern and the same connecting words, none of its other content words. Put [square brackets] around the few words it shares with the working version as they are (the frame they can borrow, at most four), never around the words that change.
The writer may write to you in any language; whatever they write in, everything you write for them is in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China).
Reply with JSON only: {"plan":"","example":""}

result.text: {"plan":"你的写法里，前半句“没有再去”和后面“他选择了……”的转折都可以留着，问题只在表示时间的那个短语。保留“在……的时候”这个结构，但要把修饰词放在表示夜里的名词前面，让整个时间短语指向月亮石那次的夜晚。","example":"Tom didn't [try] [again] [on] a rainy morning; he just took the bus instead."}
